title: His musician father Boss and his mother who played guitar
summary: Rene describes his father as a born string player and repairer and his mother playing guitar and singing; Slow Drag knew his father, called Boss, and Rene recalls a childhood chase. He also boasts of his triple tom-tom solo on Caravan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anybody, anybody you want to talk about. We'd like to know about you first. Well. And your family, you know. Anybody else in your family played, other than your brother, and you?

Well my daddy, my daddy was, he was a born musician. He used to work for Roy Lyre years ago. I understand he was the first man to put the foil in the ghetto. That's what I understand. He played ghetto, in other words he played all string instruments. Then he could repair stringing. He could make manly the ghettos. He was that way. He was a pretty good musician. That's all I can tell you about him.

My mother used to play the ghetto. I remember she used to play the ghetto and she used to sing. Well that's the time they began to cook them. The girl called it cow and it's turtle. But these, you know, when they get full of their little wine and turtles, they'd sit down. We'd play the band and she'd play the ghetto. And we'd sit out on the floor and sing, you know what I mean, until we'd get to sleep. And that was it. That's all I remember that.
Did he play jazz, what you call ragtime? Or was he strictly a reader or what?
No, I don't think he was a reader. I just think he just, this ability, this man just had that in here. According to what, I tell you a fella that kind of know him, but you know Slowdrag?

Well he used to, my daddy was, he used to come to be in what they call a wine head. And he used to bum on Espe, on the domain in Viro, and he used to call it Boss. But I mean a lot of them old heads, they're gone. But Slowdrag knows something about my daddy, by the name of Boss. Well that's the place he used to hang out every day. A better fella fell right in his footsteps. Samway hanging in the bottom, just like that. And he took the harvest, you know, and he died. Another foe, another word, he died from an elixir police hit him, you know. Never forget that boy, he was running. He was running me about 15 or 20 blocks, maybe more than that. He was running me for about a half hour. And he was saying, Blue, he's calling me the devil. He's calling my brother Angel. I'm my brother Drake just like you. He called me Angel. And he's calling me Blue, Blue, catch that devil man. And I know about to be the soul as well. That's right. But I tell you though, most of all the boys, I'll tell you, there ain't nobody ever that played Caravan like I did. Caravan. Man, I had a triple solo on that thing. It was just as nice and smooth, and a tom-tom and a rack, see. One of them gong racks. Then I had another tom-tom and I was making triplets. And I played that solo and it just, it was a beautiful. Let's see. Let's see if I... I just can't get that rhythm again, you know what I mean? But everybody said I really played that.
